standard_prerequisites.name: At-worst-nodal schemes of relative dimension one and contractions of exceptional curves
standard_prerequisites.statement: A scheme of relative dimension one over a discrete valuation ring is at-worst-nodal when its singularities are ordinary double points whose branches are smooth, equivalently when it is smooth except at finitely many points where the local equation is the standard node; a curve over a field is nodal when it is smooth except for such double points, and smoothness of a morphism of relative dimension one at a point is tested by the regularity of the local ring combined with separability of the residue extension. An exceptional curve of the first kind is a smooth rational curve of self-intersection minus one, and it may be contracted to a regular surface. The author's own lemmas of the chapter and the quoted results of the Algebra, Curves, Morphisms and Resolution of Surfaces chapters are the allowed inputs.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted lemma is the blowdown half of the resolution procedure of the semistable reduction section: it keeps the class of at-worst-nodal schemes stable under the contractions performed in the resolution of the special fibre.

core_obligations: Understand the contracted curve: the curve being contracted is an exceptional curve of the first kind on the special fibre, so it is a smooth rational curve meeting the rest of the fibre in the way recorded by the chapter's section on minus-one curves (source lines 6322-6330).

Analyse the contraction locally at the singular points: away from the contracted curve the contraction is an isomorphism, so the only points whose local structure can change are those on the contracted curve, and at each of them the local equation of the resulting scheme is computed from the local equation of the node and the blowing down (source lines 6330-6345).

Verify the nodal description of the result: at each of those points the local ring of the contracted scheme is either regular or an ordinary double point, which the proof checks by combining the regularity criterion with the separability of the residue extension, so the result is again at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one (source lines 6345-6352).
Conclude the statement: the contraction therefore keeps the class of at-worst-nodal schemes of relative dimension one, which is the assertion (source lines 6352-6355).

proof_roadmap.step: Identify the contracted curve and record its local behaviour.
Compute the local structure of the contraction at the points of the contracted curve.
Check that every local ring is regular or an ordinary double point.
Conclude that the contracted scheme is at-worst-nodal of relative dimension one.
